title: Seat Time vs. Mastery
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Calculate how many of twenty students master a fixed-length course and how many hours the early finishers sit idle, then compare with a mastery-based schedule.

educational.topic: Seat time, the Carnegie unit, and mastery
learningObjectives: The learner will calculate, for a fixed course length, how many of twenty students master the course and how many hours the early finishers sit idle, correctly answering three of three prediction questions.
prerequisites: Seat time, the Carnegie unit, mastery, and hours needed to master, from Chapter 3.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Calculate first, then explore a parameter
keyQuestions: How many students master a fixed-length course?
How many hours do the early finishers sit idle?
commonMisconceptions: A fixed course length gives every student the same chance to learn
Students who finish early are using the extra time productively
Allowing different times means the course takes more total time
assessmentOpportunities: With a 150-hour course, how many master it and how many idle hours result?
How many master a 200-hour course, and at what cost?
Does a mastery-based schedule take more total time?

controls.name: Q1, Q2, Q3 boxes
controls.description: Type the three answers with the length locked at 150 hours.

controls.name: Check answers
controls.description: Checks all unanswered questions. Two attempts each.

controls.name: Length slider
controls.description: Sets the course length from 60 to 300 hours after the questions are checked.

controls.name: Mastery-based view
controls.description: Shows every student taking exactly the hours they need.
